note: Matches the money and the starting-point tests cleanly. 'Income' is confirmed in his own words — 'I have, I definitely have the money' and 'financially, I'm in a much better place now' — alongside a premium gym membership, a chiropractor, a booked jiu-jitsu camp and a Europe trip. 'Good to great' is the clearest example in the batch: he is at roughly 15% body fat chasing the last few percent and wants to go from performing well at jiu-jitsu to being 'an absolute killer'. Plainly not deconditioned. He misses 'successful' as the ICP states it: 29 years old, an employed digital marketing and SEO salesperson, not a business owner or physician or obviously equivalent, though the rep addressed him as 'you're a business guy'. He misses 'neglected health' outright and in the opposite direction — the rep opened the call by saying so: 'clearly, you're not someone who needs to be convinced that fitness matters.' He trains six or more times a week across four disciplines; health is the least neglected part of his life. Judged against the criteria as written this is edge, and the fact that it closed is the finding: the buying population continues to be wider than the stated ICP, and here it is younger and more athletic than the ICP describes rather than less.
